newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares likely to remain under pressure.
newsitem.headline: German shares likely to remain under pressure.

text.p: German shares, which fell nearly two percent in bourse trade on Thursday, will likely remain under pressure in the near-term as dealers decide whether the losses are the start of a new correction.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 65.59 points at 3,349.81 points and had slightly extended the losses in post-bourse IBIS trade to 3,342.24 points.

Traders said the losses were not particularly dramatic since the DAX has gained some 20 percent in the last 10 weeks and a bout of profit-taking has long been anticipated, with one dealer saying the losses were "healthy" for the market.
Despite 26 of the 30 shares in the DAX index posting losses in the bourse session, traders noted gains in telephone monopoly Deutsche Tekelom and carmaker BMW AG that bucked the trend.
Telekom ended trade up 1.20 marks at 36.85 marks after hitting a new high at 37 marks. BMW shares hit a new record at 1,312 marks and ended trade up 23.50 marks at 1,291 marks.

But many shares were lower, including chemical shares such as Hoechst AG that initially kept up decline from Wednesday tied to disappointment over the shelving of plans for Hoechst to list its HMR pharmaceuticals unit on the bourse.
Hoechst shares, which fell 10 percent on Wednesday, ended bourse trade down 1.65 marks at 68.80 marks but reversed course in IBIS trade to gain 26 pfennigs at 69.40 marks.
Other chemical shares, including Bayer AG, BASF AG and Schering AG, were also lower.
Shares in engineering group Deutz AG fell as 12 marks before ending down 85 pfennigs at 12.90 marks.

Deutz was under pressure after surging in recent days after a report in Germany's Platow Brief saying the company, formerly known as Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG, would return to a profit this year. Deutz plans to release its results on May 15.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG ended down 23.50 marks at 928 marks despite its Audi luxury unit confirming a Wall Street Journal report saying Audi was contemplating a U.S. plant site.
